description: Prolog/Datalog exporter — projects the canonical TSV graph into engine-agnostic logical facts and ships runnable rule sets and example queries for both SWI-Prolog (interactive research querying via pyswip) and Souffle (high-performance bulk Datalog), enabling symbolic inference over the cultural network. This is the least-charted path; treat as original engineering.

userStories.title: Add the datalog exporter module and define the fact model
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a canonical, engine-neutral fact representation before targeting any specific engine.
acceptanceCriteria: Create src/culturescrape/datalog/__init__.py and define a Fact dataclass (predicate, args, optional source)
Document the predicate schema in docs/datalog.md: node/3+, instance_of/2, rel/3 (or typed predicates per :TYPE), and dimension facts (time_start/2, located_in/2, descends_from/2, ...)
Provide a function to safely render an atom (quoting/escaping identifiers and string literals validly for Prolog and Datalog)
Tests pass (pytest) for atom escaping incl. quotes, spaces, and unicode
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Map node TSV rows to facts
userStories.description: As a developer, I want every node row to become well-formed facts so entities exist in the logic program.
acceptanceCriteria: Each node emits node(Csid, Type, Name) plus one fact per populated dimension column (e.g. time_start(Csid, Year), located_at(Csid, Lat, Lon), language_code(Csid, Code))
csids are turned into valid lowercase atoms or quoted atoms deterministically; mapping is reversible-documented
Null/empty columns emit no fact (no nulls in the logic program)
Tests pass (pytest) mapping a fixture node file to the expected fact set
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Map edge TSV rows to facts
userStories.description: As a developer, I want every edge to become a relation fact so the graph structure is in logic.
acceptanceCriteria: Each edge emits a typed predicate per :TYPE (e.g. located_in(A,B), derived_from(A,B)) and also a generic rel(Type,A,B) for uniform queries
Predicate names are derived from :TYPE via a documented, collision-free lowercasing scheme
Edge weight/confidence is exposed via an optional companion fact (e.g. rel_conf(Type,A,B,Conf))
Tests pass (pytest) mapping a fixture edge file to expected facts
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Emit a SWI-Prolog program (.pl)
userStories.description: As a researcher, I want a loadable Prolog file so I can query the network interactively.
acceptanceCriteria: Write facts to a .pl file with appropriate :- discontiguous/:- dynamic declarations so SWI-Prolog loads it without warnings
File loads cleanly via swipl in a smoke test (skipped automatically if swipl is not installed, with the skip reason logged)
A header comment documents the predicate schema
Tests pass (pytest): the generated .pl parses; the swipl load test passes or is skipped
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Emit a Souffle program (.dl) with type declarations
userStories.description: As a data miner, I want a Souffle datalog file so I can run high-performance bulk inference.
acceptanceCriteria: Generate a .dl file with .decl declarations for every predicate, .input/.output directives, and facts loaded from generated .facts TSV files (Souffle's native format)
souffle compiles/runs the program in a smoke test (skipped automatically if souffle is not installed, with the skip reason logged)
Generated .facts files reuse the strict TSV writer so they are lossless
Tests pass (pytest): generated .dl is well-formed; the souffle run test passes or is skipped
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Author a shared rule library for derived relations
userStories.description: As a researcher, I want inference rules so the logic layer adds value beyond the raw facts.
acceptanceCriteria: Define rules (in both Prolog and Souffle syntax) for: transitive descends_from (ancestor/2), transitive located_in (within_region/2), contemporary_with as symmetric closure, and an influenced_transitively/2 over derived_from/influenced_by
Each rule has a documented intended meaning and a worked example query
Rules are stored as templates so they attach to any generated program
Tests pass (pytest) checking the rule text is emitted into both .pl and .dl outputs
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Validate inference equivalence across engines on a fixture
userStories.description: As a user, I want confidence that Prolog and Souffle agree so results are trustworthy.
acceptanceCriteria: On a fixture graph, run the same query (e.g. ancestor/2 closure) in swipl and souffle and assert identical result sets
Test skips gracefully (with logged reason) if either engine is unavailable, but runs in CI when both are present
Differences, if any, are reported with the diverging tuples
Tests pass (pytest) for the equivalence check (or skip with reason)
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Add a to-datalog CLI command
userStories.description: As a user, I want one command that turns canonical TSV into a ready logic program.
acceptanceCriteria: Add `culturescrape to-datalog <dir> --engine swipl|souffle|both --rules --out <dir>`
Command emits facts (+ rules when --rules) for the selected engine(s) and prints a load/run hint
Running on a fixture dataset produces a .pl and/or .dl that passes the relevant well-formedness test
Tests pass (pytest) invoking the CLI for each engine option
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Ship example logic queries and document the workflow
userStories.description: As a researcher, I want runnable example queries and docs so the symbolic layer is usable on day one.
acceptanceCriteria: Add datalog/examples with queries: full ancestry of a dish, all entities within a region transitively, contemporaries of an event, shortest influence chain between two artifacts
docs/datalog.md documents the predicate schema, the csid<->atom mapping, how to load in swipl, how to run in souffle, and the example queries with expected output shape
Each example references a test (or doctest) that runs it on the fixture when the engine is available
Tests pass (pytest) for the example harness (skipping engine-specific parts when unavailable)
Lint passes (ruff)
